summary: The curated subset is strongly fail-closed and generally consistent, with bounded artifact handling, explicit execution approvals, conservative scanner triage, and structured V1–V6 verification. Three medium contract gaps remain: an incomplete #4b detector, an overbroad generation prohibition on legitimate attachment assertions, and an underspecified V6 summary row.

findings.title: Parameterized toBeAttached assertions evade #4b scanning
findings.evidence: The #4b Tier 3 expression matches only the exact empty-argument form `toBeAttached()`, although the documented pattern covers positive `toBeAttached` assertions generally. Valid forms such as `toBeAttached({ timeout: 5000 })` receive no mechanical candidate, and #4b is absent from the mandatory fallback token sweep.
findings.recommendation: Match a positive `toBeAttached(` call with arbitrary bounded arguments, retain the existing negative-form exclusion, and leave contextual severity confirmation to Phase 2.

findings.title: Generation rule rejects a documented legitimate attachment contract
findings.evidence: The forbidden-pattern table directs `toBeAttached()` to `toBeVisible()` and exempts only negative and dynamically injected cases. The authoritative pattern contract also recognizes attachment as meaningful when a CSS-hidden element must remain in the DOM, so generation guidance can replace a semantically correct assertion with a different visibility contract.
findings.recommendation: Permit `toBeAttached()` whenever DOM attachment itself is the approved outcome, including CSS-hidden persistence, and forbid it only when attachment is weak evidence for a visibility or removal promise.

findings.title: Condensed V6 proof omits fresh-context separation
findings.evidence: The cross-framework proof table describes V6 as rerunning `e2e-reviewer` after repair, while the generator contract requires a distinct fresh-context, read-only reviewer and explicitly rejects inline self-review as PASS. The condensed row can therefore be followed without the separation needed for a valid V6 verdict.
findings.recommendation: Change the V6 proof cells to require rerunning `e2e-reviewer` in a distinct fresh-context, read-only actor or process that did not write or repair the candidate.

limitations: Packet-only static review; no commands, tests, benchmarks, holdouts, or runtime probes were executed.
The curated subset omits referenced helpers, scanner rules, fixtures, manifests, and CI test implementations, so their behavior and parity cannot be assessed.
This is not full product coverage, skill-accuracy measurement, independent ground truth, human or sealed review, or remote model attestation.
